s: This is Planet Money from NPR.
这是NPR的星球货币。
Announcer
There's this type of video that the Department of Defense keeps putting out that I have found fascinating.
美国国防部不断发布的视频，我觉得很迷人。
Nick Fountain
In one, shot in the Indian Ocean earlier this year, a US military helicopter is approaching an enormous ship while someone makes an ultimatum over the radio.
在今年早些时候在印度洋拍摄的其中之一，一架美国军用直升机接近一个巨大的船只，有人在电台上发出最后通话。
SPEAKER 1: Motor vessel Majestic X, we intend to conduct a boarding of your vessel.
发言人1号：机器舰 Majestic X，我们打算登上你的船。
"We intend to conduct a boarding of your vessel."
"我们打算登上你的船。
Fountain
And the visual accompanied by this is stunning-- a wide, open ocean, deep blue sea, pretty calm.
一个宽的，开放的海洋，深蓝色的海洋，相当平静。
And at the center of the frame is the Majestic X, this giant, hulking oil tanker.
在框架的中心是 Majestic X，这个巨大的油轮。
On its deck, you can see the pipes they use for loading oil.
在甲板上，你可以看到它们用于加载石油的管道。
And near the back of the ship, in front of enormous smokestacks, you can see the ship's bridge, the command center.
在船后面，在巨大的烟台前，你可以看到船的桥，指挥中心。
Cut to a shot of two helicopters hovering directly over the deck of the ship, maybe 20 feet up, and a naval boarding crew jumping out of these helicopters, rappelling down huge ropes.
两架直升机直接悬浮在船甲板上，也许高20英尺，一个海军登上船员从这些直升机中跳出来，下了巨大的绳子。
Next, they're walking towards the ship's bridge, guns pointed towards, presumably, the crew, and then, the video is over.
接下来，他们走向船的桥梁，枪支指向了船员，然后，视频结束。
They don't show us exactly what it looks like when US forces enter the control room.
当美国军队进入控制室时，他们并没有告诉我们什么样子。
But we know from statements the US put out that they seized this ship.
但我们从美国的声明中知道他们没收了这艘船。
It is one of many such videos of many such operations this year.
这是今年许多行动的许多视频之一。
The American military has seized oil tankers with fuel that was headed from Venezuela and ships headed out of Iran.
美国军方没收了来自委内瑞拉的油轮，飞船从伊朗出发。
The Department of Defense has said that this is all in an effort to disrupt illicit networks.
美国国防部表示，这一切都是为了破坏非法网络。
And I've been wondering, once the US military seizes these massive oil tankers, what are they doing with them?
我一直在想，一旦美国军队占领了这些巨大的油轮，他们用它们做什么？。
Well, it turns out, once they have them, they are trying to sell them, liquidate the ships and what's on board.
结果，一旦他们得到了它们，他们试图卖掉它们，清算船只和船上的东西。
But that could take years.
但这可能需要数年时间。
It's a very tedious legal process, especially if you compare it to what we used to do in the way past.
这是一个非常乏味的法律程序，特别是如果你把它比较到我们以前所做的。

Back in the era of wooden chips and peg legs depicted by a burly Russell Crowe in the movie Master and Commander, warring countries could seize ships, or, as they called them, prizes, and auction the ships and their contents off in a matter of days or weeks, in what they called prize courts.
在电影"大师和指挥官"中，鲁塞尔·克罗 (Russell Crowe) 描绘的木头片和脚时代，
And I shit you not, the US is thinking of bringing this back.
我不给你，美国正在考虑把它带回来。
SPEAKER 2: For England, for home, and for the prize!
为了英格兰，为了家，为了奖励！
For Planet Money, for podcasts, and for the prize, I'm Nick Fountain.
为了星球钱，为了播客，为了奖项，我是尼克喷泉。
The Trump administration has nostalgia for many bygone eras, but this may be one of the stranger things they're hoping to bring back.
特朗普政府对过去的许多时代怀念，但这可能是他们希望带回来的更奇怪的事情之一。
They're busy resurrecting a set of laws that were once the justification for state-sponsored pirates, otherwise known as privateers.
他们忙于重建一套曾经是政府赞助的海盗的正当性，其他称之为骑士。
If they have their way, it'll become a lot easier for them to auction off the ships of their enemies and everything on board without a million trips to the courthouse.
如果他们有自己的方式，他们会更容易拍卖敌人的船只和船上的一切，
How are they going to pull this off?
他们如何做到这一点？
Well, swab the decks, hoist the burgee, hold fast, and keep your ears to the wind.
好吧，扫一扫地板，举起子，坚持着，让你听风。
That's right.
这是真的。
Today on the show, we're talking warfare on the open seas.
今天的节目中，我们正在谈论开放海上的战争。
When I heard the US might be bringing back this Captain Hook-era legal regime, the system to sell off booty, called prize law, I started calling around to see if it was for real.
当我听说美国可能会恢复这次船长胡克时代的法律制度，销售掠夺的系统，我开始打电话来看看这是真的吗？。
I spent weeks going back and forth with the Navy, who eventually confirmed it with a statement.
我花了几周时间与海军交往，他们最终通过一份声明证实了这一点。
They said, quote, "Prize law has ancient roots in maritime law and provides the framework to condemn, return, or dispose of maritime property seized in conflict."
他们说："奖项法在海事法中具有古老的根源，返回或处置冲突中没收的海事财产"
In other words, they're potentially doing this.
换句话说，他们可能会这样做。

And I talked with a couple of Justice Department officials who asked that we not use their names because they were not authorized to speak publicly about this, who confirmed, yes, they were really working with the Navy on this.
我和司法部的一些官员交谈，他们要求我们不要使用他们的名字，因为他们没有授权公开谈论这个问题，
I even talked with the actual judge tasked with standing up a modern-day prize court.
我甚至和真正的法官交谈，
But before we get into the details of how this might work, let us step back and ask, what is happening with the ships now?
但在我们详细介绍如何运作之前，让我们退一步问，现在船只发生了什么？
Like, what is the system we currently have?
我们目前的系统是什么？
Well, to help figure that out, we called up Annie Brett, law professor at the University of Florida, lover of maritime law and of boats.
为了帮助解决这个问题，我们打电话给安妮·布雷特，在佛罗里达大学的法学教授，爱海洋法和船只。
Do you own a boat now?
你现在拥有船吗？
I-- of course, I own a boat, yes.
我当然拥有船只，是的。
Annie Brett
[LAUGHS] I'm a sailor.
我是一个水手。
So prior to my legal career, I was a captain of sailing large sailing vessels.
因此，在我成为律师之前，我曾是大型帆船的船长。
Nice flex.
漂亮的柔性。
Fountain
We asked Annie, so, wait, if the government seizes a ship these days, what do they do with it?
我们问安妮，等待，如果政府今天抓住一艘船，他们用它做什么？。
Where does it go?
它去哪里？
What happens to the oil?
油怎么样呢？
And she was like, oh, well, it is slow.
她说，，这是缓慢的。
Prosecutors have to use a process similar to the one they used when they, say, seize a drug dealer's drugs or their G-wagon-- civil asset forfeiture.
检察官必须使用类似于他们使用的过程，当他们，说，抓住毒品经销商的毒品或他们的G-wagon--民事资产没收。
Not as sweet a name as prize law.
不像奖项法一样甜蜜的名字。
It's more like the "very meticulous way the government is legally allowed to take your stuff" law.
它更像是"政府可以合法地拿走你的东西"的法律。
Basically, the government files a complicated lawsuit against the property.
基本上，政府对财产起了复杂的诉讼。

Civil forfeiture is a process that basically allows anyone that has any kind of claim against the vessel, like the owner, the people that are buying the cargo-- any type of claim against the vessel can come into this forfeiture proceeding and make arguments about what they're entitled to.
公民没收是基本上允许任何人对船有任何形式的索赔，就像所有者，购买货物的人 - - 任何类型的对船只的索赔都可以进入这个没收程序。
Brett
Like, anyone who thinks they have some ownership claim to the ship or deserve part of the profits from selling it, they can make their case.
任何认为他们拥有船只的权利或应该从销售中获得部分利的人都能证明自己的观点。
Fountain
So because of this, it's like a typical, very-- just very lengthy lawsuit before the ship can actually be auctioned off.
所以，由于这个原因，这就像一个典型的，在这艘船被拍卖之前，很长一段诉讼。
Brett
So it's not fast.
所以这不是快的。
Take, for example, the case of the ship we talked about at the beginning of the show, the Majestic X. It is kind of a perfect example for how not fast this current system we have is.
举例来说，我们在节目开始时谈到的飞船，Majestic X. 它是我们目前系统的速度不快的完美的例子。
Fountain
Two days after US forces seized it in the Indian Ocean, the DOJ filed a court case against the ship and its oil.
在美国军队在印度洋捕获后两天，司法部向该船及其石油提起了诉讼。
They were trying to use civil asset forfeiture to sell off the ship and the oil inside quickly.
他们试图利用民事资产被没收，快速出售船和石油。
But a judge made that hard.
但一位法官使得这变得很难。

She wrote, kind of dismissively, quote, "To put it plainly, the United States is asking to sell the property in secret to a buyer of its choice before any potential claimant has an opportunity to object."
她写道，有点轻视，简单地说，在任何潜在的索赔者有机会反对之前，美国要求秘密向其选择的买家出售财产
The US had to notify the Iranian national oil company and the ship's suspected owners.
美国不得不通知伊朗国家石油公司和该船的嫌疑所有者。
And then, out of the woodwork came a claim from a group of hundreds of people who were victims of Iranian terrorism, who asked for at least a cut of the proceeds from the sale and for a jury trial.
后来，来自伊朗恐怖主义的数百名受害者的一群人，要求至少从销售收益中削减一分。
Meanwhile, this boat was just sitting there, full of oil.
与此同时，这艘船只是坐在那里，充满了石油。
And as anyone who's ever had a friend who's bought a boat, only to regret it immediately, can tell you, no boat is cheap to maintain.
作为任何曾经有过买船的朋友，只是要立刻悔过，可以告诉你，任何船都不便宜维护。
It is expensive to have a boat, and to run a boat, and to meet, like, all the things that you would expect, yes.
拥有一艘船，运营一艘船，满足你期望的一切都是昂贵的。
Brett
You know from experience.
你从经验中知道。
Fountain
Boats are very expensive.
船票非常昂贵。
Brett
And boats-- I mean, this is the thing that comes up, right, in these contexts, is, like, boats sitting is very, very expensive.
而船只--我想，在这种情况下，出现的问题是，坐船非常，非常昂贵。
You are losing a lot of money while your boat is sitting, and the government is figuring out what to do with it.
在船上坐着的时候，你会损失很多钱，政府正在找出该用什么。
The ideal thing for a commercial shipping vessel is just to be always on the move?
一艘商业航运船的理想选择是，总是在移动？
Fountain
Always on the move.
总是在移动。
Brett
Always on the move, yeah.
总是在移动，是的。
OK, now imagine an oil tanker full of a liquid that causes some of the worst environmental disasters known to humans.
现在想象一下，一个装满液体的油轮会造成人类所知的最严重的环境灾害。
Fountain
How expensive would that be to maintain?
维护的费用有多高？
Well, we know.
我们知道。

A Justice Department official told the court that the US had spent $42 million on custody, maintenance, and repairs for the Majestic X in the first month and a half after it was seized, even though the government says the street value for the ship was less than $3 million.
美国司法部官员告诉法庭，在被没收后的第一个半个月里，尽管政府说，这艘船的街头价值不到300万美元。
At the time we're recording this, the case has dragged on for nearly seven months.
在我们录制时，这起案件已经持续了近7个月。
And still, this ship and the oil are in the government's hands.
尽管如此，这艘船和石油都在政府手中。
In other words, this whole thing, the whole process of civil asset forfeiture, is cumbersome on purpose, right?
换句话说，这一切，整个民事资产被没收的过程，是故意繁重的，对吧？
Because we don't want the government seizing private property willy-nilly.
因为我们不希望政府随意没收私人财产。
But also, for the government, it is a long, expensive, and inefficient process.
但对于政府来说，这是一个漫长，昂贵，不高效的过程。
And so you could see why the government might want to turn towards this antiquated prize law, so old that even studied maritime lawyers don't know too much about it.
所以你可以理解为什么政府可能会转向这个过时的奖金法，这么古老，甚至有学历的海上律师都不知道太多。
Is it something that you learn in law school?
这是你在法学院学到的东西吗？
No, absolutely not.
绝对没有。
Brett
Why would you learn prize law?
你为什么要学习奖金法？
No one has used it in 50 years, 100 years.
没有人用过50年，100年。
It would be-- it's irrelevant at this point-- or so we thought.
在这个时候，它是无关紧要的，或者我们以为是这样。
So we thought.
这就是我们想的。
Fountain
So we thought.
这就是我们想的。
Brett
Luckily for us, there is someone who has spent a good portion of their life learning about prize law-- Nathan Perl-Rosenthal, who, if you prod him enough, he will admit--
幸运的是，有一个人，他一生中大部分时间都学会了奖金法，如果你给他足够的刺激，他会承认--
Fountain
I think it's possible that I know more about prize law than anybody currently living.
我认为我可能比目前活着的人更了解奖金法。
Nathan Perl-Rosenthal
Yeah, there's a lot of dead guys who know about it, right?
是的，很多死人都知道，对吧？
Fountain
There were a lot of dead guys who knew about it, including some dead guys who we're still reading today.
有很多死人知道这一点，包括一些死人，我们今天还在读。
Perl-Rosenthal
Great.
很棒的。
Fountain
Nathan is a maritime historian.
纳森是一位海事历史学家。
He works at Harvard.
他在哈佛工作。
Do you come from a boating family?
你来自一个船员家庭吗？
A lot of sailing?
很多航行？
Not at all.
绝对没有。
Perl-Rosenthal
I get terribly seasick.
我非常生海病。
No way.
没有办法。
Fountain
Oh, yeah.
是的，是的。
Perl-Rosenthal
[LAUGHS]
现在，我们要做什么呢？
Fountain
Totally.
完全是这样。
Perl-Rosenthal
Totally.
完全是这样。
We didn't want to talk to him about that, though.
我们不想和他谈论这一点。
Fountain
We wanted to talk to him about the world from which prize law came, to understand what it was about that world that the Trump administration wants to bring back.
我们想跟他谈谈奖金法来自的世界，了解特朗普政府想要恢复的世界。
Nathan told us the heyday of prize was the 17th and 18th centuries, when the European powers were regularly fighting wars with each other on the high seas.
纳森告诉我们，奖金的盛时期是17世纪和18世纪，当欧洲大国经常在公海上互相争战时。
But they had limited naval power, so they leaned on prize-taking, or privateering.
但他们的海军力量有限，所以他们依赖于获奖。
What is that?
这是什么？
It's essentially piracy with permission.
这基本上是有许可的海盗行为。
Perl-Rosenthal
[LAUGHS]
现在，我们要做什么呢？
Fountain
I mean, a better way of saying it, really, is that piracy is prize-taking without permission.
实际上，更好地说，海盗是没有许可的获奖。
Perl-Rosenthal
Uh-huh.
哈哈。
Fountain
But the acts are almost identical.
但这些行为几乎是一样的。
Perl-Rosenthal
One man's pirate is another man's prize-taker, another man's privateer.
一个人的海盗是另一个人的获奖者，另一个人的私人。
Fountain
Absolutely.
绝对。
Perl-Rosenthal
Absolutely.
绝对。
And what prize law did was make sure that these kind of savage dudes didn't operate entirely with impunity and steal every ship they saw.
而奖金法所做的就是确保这些野蛮人不完全不受惩罚，他们偷走了所有的船只。
Fountain
It provided a set of rules that they had to follow if they didn't want to be criminals.
如果他们不想成为罪犯，他们必须遵守一套规则。
Here's how it worked.
这就是它运作的方式。
At the beginning of any given war, the king or queen put out a proclamation saying, it's go time.
在任何战争开始时，国王或女王发出宣告说，现在是时候去的。
I'm now authorizing any rich patriot with a boat to put cannon on their ships and essentially become my bonus navy.
我现在授权任何有船的富国爱好者，基本上成为我的奖金海军。
Go out, seize enemy ships, and keep a portion of the spoils, if you follow the rules.
你们要出去，夺取敌方的船只，要遵守规则，要留下一些战利物。
Like, you got to have insurance.
你必须有保险。
You got to get a surety bond to pay any claims if you do bad things.
如果你做了坏事，你必须获得保证券来支付任何索赔。
You got to carry what's called a commission.
你必须承担所谓的佣金。
What's a commission?
一个佣金是什么？
It's the thing that makes you not a pirate.
这就是让你不是海盗的原因。
Perl-Rosenthal
Yeah, the privateering commission has a piece of paper that says, so and so is hereby authorized to cruise.
是的，私人化委员会有一张纸上写着，所以，所以被授权巡航。
Here are the, you know, specifications.
这里是，你知道的，规格。
And then it's signed by a-- you know, an official.
然后由一位官员签署。
This piece of paper is incredibly powerful.
这张纸是非常强大的。
Fountain
It gives captains the right to take enemy ships, or, sometimes, even ships carrying stuff to or from their enemy, or even ships crewed by the enemy.
它赋予船长权夺取敌方船只，或者，有时，甚至是向敌方运送物品的船只，甚至是敌方机组的船只。
With this piece of paper, you were good to go.
随着这张纸张，你已经准备好了。
All right, so you go out.
好吧，你出去吧。
Perl-Rosenthal
You go to a place where you think you're likely to find enemy ships.
你去一个你认为你可能会找到敌方的船只的地方。
And you get lucky, and you find one, right?
如果你有幸运，你会找到一个，对吗？
You raise your flag, fire a warning shot, and the other ship is supposed to stop.
你举起旗，发出警告射击，另一个船应该停下来。
Most of the time, Nathan says, they did stop.
纳森说，他们大部分时间都停了下来。
Fountain
It was the safest choice.
这是最安全的选择。
And here's where the rules get very specific.
在这里，规则变得非常具体。
The privateering captain rows over to the ship he's hoping to take as prize, boards it, and essentially gathers a bunch of evidence.
骑士船长排到他希望拿到的船上，上船，基本上收集了一堆证据。
And he very quickly, somewhere from 15 minutes to an hour, kind of looks everything over.
他很快就说，在某个地方15分钟到一个小时，一样看着一切。
Perl-Rosenthal
He looks over the ship's papers, and he looks over the crew.
他看着船上的文件，他看着船员。
What he does is, he talks to them, and he tries to figure out what their native language is, to figure out if they're enemy subjects or neutrals.
他试图弄清楚他们的母语是什么，弄清楚他们是敌人还是中立。
And basically, what he's trying to do is, he's trying to figure out how linked to the enemy this ship, or its cargo, or its crew is.
他试图做的是，他试图弄清楚这艘船是如何与敌人联系的，或其货物，或其船员。
Fountain

If he finds reason to think that the ship, or the cargo, or anything might be valid prize, he takes most of the crew of that ship off and puts them on his ship, and puts part of his crew on that ship, OK, as what's called a prize crew.
如果他有理由认为这艘船，或是货物，或任何可能是有效的奖励，他把船上的大部分船员赶出去，把他们送上他的船上，他把他的船员中的一部分放在船上，好吧，作为所谓的奖品团队。
Perl-Rosenthal
That captain sends the ship and all the evidence he collected to port, to be presented to a prize court.
那个船长把船和收集到的证据都送到港口，在奖金法庭上。
Fountain
And this is the part of prize law that the Trump administration is working on resuscitating.
而这是特朗普政府正在努力恢复的奖金法的一部分。
Not the privateering bonus navy part, the prize court, which can also be used by the real navy.
没有私人化奖金海军部分，皇家海军也可以使用的奖金法院。

Back in the day, once a captain sent all that evidence to the court, the prize court judge would ask a bunch of standardized questions to the crew and very quickly figure out a way to deal with the ship and its contents.
在过去，一旦一个船长把所有这些证据送到法庭，奖金法院的法官会向船员提出一堆标准问题。
They'd look over the evidence and usually say, yeah, this is a valid prize.
他们会检查证据，通常说，是的，这是一个有效的奖励。
It can be auctioned off to savvy merchants who might score a sweet deal on gold, or gin, or chestnuts, or, sadly, enslaved people.
它可以拍卖给聪明的商人，他们可能会买黄金，酒，栗子，或者，不幸的是，奴隶。
Yeah.
是的，是的。
And then the proceeds would be split amongst the captain, the crew, investors, and of course, the state.
